stem: Angiotensin I becomes biologically active after cleavage by which enzyme?

options.label: A
options.text: Renin enzyme acting on circulating angiotensinogen
options.misconception: The angiotensinogen-cleaving enzyme is being confused with ACE.
options.explanation: Renin produces angiotensin I from angiotensinogen; ACE converts angiotensin I to II.

options.label: B
options.text: Pulmonary ACE turning angiotensin I into form II
options.misconception: None; ACE from the lungs converts angiotensin I to active angiotensin II.
options.explanation: Angiotensin I is converted to angiotensin II by ACE from the lungs.

options.label: C
options.text: Adrenal enzyme synthesizing aldosterone steroid hormone
options.misconception: A downstream steroid enzyme is being credited with I→II conversion.
options.explanation: Aldosterone synthase makes aldosterone; ACE performs the I→II conversion.

options.label: D
options.misconception: The kinin system is being confused with ACE conversion.
options.explanation: Kallikrein is not the enzyme that converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II.

options.label: E
options.text: Pepsin enzyme digesting dietary angiotensin peptides
options.misconception: A digestive protease is being substituted for pulmonary ACE.
options.explanation: Pepsin digests dietary protein; ACE in the lungs activates angiotensin II.

context: Learning objective: identify ACE from the lungs as the enzyme converting angiotensin I to II.
